inputs.text: On 25 March 2026, Foreign Minister Roberto Álvarez and OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann signed an agreement in Paris to design the Dominican Republic’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy, with President Luis Abinader witnessing it. That could be a useful step, but adopting global standards is not the same as changing the conditions that let corruption and unequal access to power persist. The strategy will matter only if it brings real accountability and protects people who bear the costs of abuse—not just institutional credibility on the international stage.
